newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul, Aero Int'l to develop passenger planes.
newsitem.headline: Seoul, Aero Int'l to develop passenger planes.

text.p: South Korea will team up with Europe's Aero International Regional (AIR) to develop mid-sized passenger planes, domestic media reported on Thursday.

The Joona-Ang Ilbo said a consortium of South Korean aerospace companies, led by Samsung Aerospace Ind, and AIR agreed to a $1.2 billion project which will produce mid-sized aircraft from 2001. It said the memorandum of understanding would be signed on Friday.

Korean companies would have a 30-40 percent stake, while AIR, a multinational company composed of St Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale of France, British Aerospace Plc of Britain and Alenia of Italy, will hold 50 percent.
The paper said the two parties would negotiate terms of technology transfers and other details until June when the financial contract was scheduled.
It said they would develop 70-seat, 58 and 84-seat planes, with test aircraft completed by next year.
South Korea will have assembly lines by around 2007 and be responsible for completing production of planes and distributing them in the Asian market, it said.
